slides.headline:
22,000 Korean cafes
would rather you brought a cup.
slides.subline: A voluntary pact with the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment starts this month — up to 800 won off a drink if you carry a tumbler

slides.label: The most you can save per drink for bringing your own cup — roughly 300 to 400 won knocked off at the till by the shop, topped up with points from the government's Carbon Neutrality Action Points scheme. About 0.60 US dollars
slides.note: Sources: World Coffee Portal, 16 July 2026 — agreement terms, the 300-400 won store discount, the September 2026 start date · The Korea Times, 14 July 2026 — up to 800 won combining store discounts with carbon neutrality points, 23 chains, 22,000 stores · Checked 16 September 2026

items.t: Drink in, and it should come in a real cup
items.d: Businesses that signed up have agreed to move to reusable cups for anything consumed on the premises. If you sit down, expect ceramic or glass rather than paper

items.t: Bring a tumbler, get money off
items.d: Up to 800 won per drink — a 300 to 400 won discount at the shop's own discretion, plus government carbon-neutrality points. The shop sets its own figure, so it varies

items.t: Straws only if you ask for one
items.d: Single-use straws stop being handed out by default. You request one at the kiosk or from staff. Reporting describes this as applying regardless of what the straw is made of
The routine of nesting a plastic cup inside a paper one for insulation is part of what signatories pledged to stop, alongside a phase-out of PET cans

slides.title:
Korea has
tried this before.
slides.body:
The pact is voluntary. It is an agreement between a ministry and a list of companies, not a law, and nobody is fined for ignoring it.

That matters, because the mandatory version kept collapsing. Rules covering paper cups and plastic straws took effect in November 2022 with a year's grace. In November 2023, before it expired, the government scrapped the paper-cup ban outright and postponed straw enforcement indefinitely, citing costs to small business owners. By mid-2024 a ministry official was quoted saying it is realistically impossible to regulate disposables.

Then in December 2025 a draft strategy proposed charging for takeaway cups. A plan, not a rule.

items.t: Assume the cafe in front of you is not covered
items.d: About 22,000 outlets signed — 23 chains including Starbucks, Ediya, Paris Baguette and McDonald's, plus roughly 150 independents. Set against the 100,729 shops Statistics Korea counted in 2022, that is a small slice. Ask, or look for a notice at the till

items.t: Seoul runs a second, separate discount
items.d: 500 won on a personal cup — 100 won off at the till from the cafe, 400 won in points from the city. It needs the Seoul Pay app and a participating shop, listed on Smart Seoul Map. Announced to run to the end of 2026, but the city says it may stop earlier if the budget is spent

items.t: The for-here-or-to-go question decides your cup
items.d: Staff will ask. Answering 'to go' when you are sitting down is how travellers end up with a paper cup at a table. A useful English search phrase is 'personal cup discount', or 'tumbler discount'

items.t: None of this makes a cafe cheap or good
items.d: A discount of a few hundred won is not a recommendation. It is worth carrying a tumbler if you were going to carry one anyway

slides.text:
This is research, not a personal visit.
Every fact here comes from a published source, checked on 16 September 2026.
slides.by:
Where sources differ we have said so rather than picking one. The Korea Times describes 23 chains with over 22,000 stores plus around 150 independent cafes; World Coffee Portal puts the total at about 22,000 outlets.
The December 2025 charge for takeaway plastic cups was a draft strategy heading to a public hearing — we have found no confirmation that it is in force, so do not budget for it.

caption:
From this month, about 22,000 cafes and fast-food outlets across Korea are meant to serve dine-in drinks in reusable cups — and to pay you up to 800 won for bringing your own tumbler.

The catch: it is a voluntary pact with the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment, not a law. Statistics Korea counted 100,729 coffee shops in the country at the end of 2022, so most of them are not covered. Look for a notice at the till, or ask.

In Seoul there is a separate 500 won personal-cup discount through the Seoul Pay app, running to the end of 2026 while the budget lasts.

Mandatory versions of this rule were introduced in 2022 and scrapped in 2023, and a December 2025 plan to charge for takeaway cups is still only a draft. We have flagged what is confirmed and what is not.

Sources in the last slide. Save it for your trip.
